newsitem.title: DUBAI: UAE protests Iran building pier on disputed island. [CORRECTED 16:30 GMT]
newsitem.headline: UAE protests Iran building pier on disputed island. [CORRECTED 16:30 GMT]

text.p: The UAE protested on Saturday to the U.N. over a pier it said Iran had built on Greater Tunb, one of three islands at the centre of a dispute between the two oil-rich Gulf countries, the official WAM news agency reported.
(Corrects name of island from Abu Musa).

WAM said the United Arab Emirates'(UAE) delegation to the U.N. addressed a letter to U.N. Secretary General Kofi Annan "which included a memorandum of protest over the pier which the foreign ministry had relayed to the Iranian embassy in Abu Dhabi".
It quoted Khaled al-Mualla, the UAE acting charge d'affaires to the U.N., as saying the letter "stressed that the Iranian measure was a flagrant violation of international law and UAE sovereignty".
Since 1992, Iran and the UAE have been at loggerheads over the islands of Abu Musa, Greater and Lesser Tunbs that are close to key oil shipping lanes at the mouth of the Gulf.
Gulf Arab states have long demanded an end to the Iranian "occupation" of the islands.
Abu Dhabi has urged Tehran to agree to take the dispute to the International Court of Justice in the Hague. But Iran has said the row should be settled through negotiations.
The Tehran government has repeatedly said the islands were "inseparable parts of Iran".
The UAE last year accused Iran of deploying offensive weapons at the three disputed islands.
